records.title: Hybrid retrieval must return traceable evidence contexts with vector, graph, fusion score metadata, and EvidencePath references.
findings: Hybrid retrieval evidence requirement remains valid, but future ADRs should avoid assuming a specific graph substrate implementation.

records.title: RLM document navigation and workflow-in-code prototypes must be read-only, bounded, and return typed draft outputs plus trajectories validated by deterministic code.
findings: Supports current architecture direction or safety constraints.

records.title: RLM graph traversal must be benchmarked against vector-only, one-hop graph expansion, and heuristic BFS before adoption recommendations are made.
findings: Supports current architecture direction or safety constraints.

records.title: Before expanding beyond M003, the system must validate current scientific KG behavior on staged real article batches of 10 documents, 20 documents, and then a one-week corpus, with analysis of graph quality at each stage.
findings: Scientific KG staged validation remains primary-domain scope; ADRs should clarify it is the proving path, not the only future KB domain.

records.title: Before scientific KG validation or scaling continues, converted paper data and chunks must satisfy an explicit graph-readiness quality contract covering conversion fidelity, normalization, chunk semantics, table/figure handling, section hierarchy, and evidence provenance.
findings: Graph-readiness quality contract remains binding for scientific papers; ADRs should separate paper-specific readiness from generic KB readiness.

records.title: Before KG import continues, chunking must produce an import-ready typed chunk package with stable IDs, source spans, parent-child lineage, content routes, quality states, deterministic annotations, and independent review evidence.
findings: Chunk import-ready package remains scientific-paper specific; ADRs should avoid treating it as universal content contract.

records.title: Before drawing broader chunking/import-readiness conclusions, validation must expand from the 10-paper gold corpus to a 30-paper deviation scan that compares distributions, outliers, missing-source rates, route/refusal patterns, and new failure modes without authorizing production KG import.
findings: 30-paper deviation scan remains paper-domain validation breadth; ADRs should keep it as primary-domain evidence, not universal-KB completeness.

records.title: Corpus validation must support an automated +10-paper iterative loop up to 100 papers, with resumable batch state, source acquisition, deviation analysis, remediation recommendations, and strict no-import/no-write safety gates.
findings: Supports current architecture direction or safety constraints.

records.title: Provide a deterministic, resumable CLI workflow for iterative +10-paper validation batches toward a 100-paper diagnostic corpus.
findings: Deterministic corpus CLI remains compatible; clarify that it is a paper-domain workflow over generic resumable evidence orchestration.

records.title: Validation batches must fill the target accepted-paper quota by drawing deterministic replacement candidates when selected papers cannot become source-ready within bounded acquisition rules.
findings: Supports current architecture direction or safety constraints.

records.title: New infrastructure must be researched, compatibility-probed, and safety-wrapped before it is enabled in the main Scientific KG process.
findings: Supports current architecture direction or safety constraints.

records.title: Provide a deterministic CLI for detecting article structure artifacts and candidate KG scaffold links from preserved paper sources without performing KG import.

records.title: MiniMax may assist article artifact detection only as a bounded structured helper with forced tool calls, local schema validation, redacted inputs, and non-authoritative outputs.

records.title: DSPy prompt optimization for artifact detection must remain gated until benchmark fixtures, metrics, and baseline MiniMax or deterministic outputs exist.
